paraphrase: Ordinary mind is one's own present awareness, uncontrived by anything, unspoiled by any (spiritual or worldly) conception; resting in it as it is, is the dharmakāya recognized.
notes: Reference from memory; the text is not available locally. Topic anchor; the widely quoted definition is recalled in substance only.

paraphrase: Gampopa gave the Mahāmudrā pointing-out, grounded in devotion and the guru's blessing and in the sūtra teaching on buddha-nature, also to disciples who had not received tantric empowerment, besides teaching it within the path of method.
notes: Reference from memory; the text is not available locally. Reported by later sources (Gö Lotsāwa, Kongtrul) rather than recalled as a quotation; low.

paraphrase: Co-emergent union: mind-as-such, co-emergent, is the dharmakāya; appearances, co-emergent, are the light of the dharmakāya; thoughts, co-emergent, are the waves of the dharmakāya.
notes: Reference from memory; the text is not available locally. Topic anchor; the triad is widely quoted in the Kagyu as Gampopa's.

paraphrase: Gampopa's assembly teachings join the Kadam graded path — renunciation, compassion and bodhicitta — with the Mahāmudrā instruction, so that the view is pointed out to a mind prepared by the path.
notes: Reference from memory; the text is not available locally. Topic anchor; low.
